rationale: The change is small, focused, and correct. It introduces a dedicated ErrorCode (LITE_LLM_LANGUAGE_VALIDATION_ERROR) for LANGUAGE_VALIDATION guardrail errors and routes them via a dict lookup with an explicit fallback to LITE_LLM_CONTENT_POLICY_VIOLATION_ERROR for all other guardrail types — preserving the previous behavior for every type not yet mapped. The fallback is intentional and well-placed. A corresponding config message and LITELLM_ERROR_FRIENDLY_MESSAGES entry are wired correctly. The new test exercises the full classify() path with the same Exception(json_str) pattern established by all prior tests in the class. Two non-blocking findings are documented below: one correctness concern (case-sensitive key matching, low observed risk given the provider schema uses uppercase throughout) and one conventions gap (missing ticket prefix in the commit message).

business_review.criterion: LANGUAGE_VALIDATION guardrail errors produce a dedicated error code, not CONTENT_POLICY_VIOLATION
business_review.notes: GUARDRAIL_ERROR_TYPE_TO_ERROR_CODE maps 'LANGUAGE_VALIDATION' -> LITE_LLM_LANGUAGE_VALIDATION_ERROR; confirmed by the new test.

business_review.criterion: Unknown guardrail error types still fall back to LITE_LLM_CONTENT_POLICY_VIOLATION_ERROR
business_review.notes: dict.get(error_type, ErrorCode.LITE_LLM_CONTENT_POLICY_VIOLATION_ERROR) preserves prior behavior for all types not in the map. Existing test for HATE_SPEECH-style guardrail continues to assert CONTENT_POLICY_VIOLATION.

business_review.criterion: User-facing message for LANGUAGE_VALIDATION is wired end-to-end
business_review.notes: LITELLM_MSG_LANGUAGE_VALIDATION added to Config; LITELLM_ERROR_FRIENDLY_MESSAGES entry added for LITE_LLM_LANGUAGE_VALIDATION_ERROR.

business_review.criterion: No regression to other error classification paths
business_review.notes: Change is confined to the GuardrailErrorModel branch of _get_error_code(); the elif/else branches for LITE_LLM_EXC_TYPE_TO_ERROR_CODE and keyword fallback are untouched.

business_review.criterion: Sanity harness passes with the change deployed
business_review.notes: 189 passed, 0 failed, 4 skipped — clean run with uvx codemie-test-harness run --marks 'api and sanity' -n 4 --reruns 3.

standards_review.standard: code-quality: type annotations on changed code
standards_review.notes: _get_error_code return type is ErrorCode | None (modern union syntax). The untyped `inner` parameter is pre-existing, not introduced by this diff.

standards_review.standard: error-handling guide: dedicated error codes per guardrail type
standards_review.notes: Pattern follows the established LITE_LLM_EXC_TYPE_TO_ERROR_CODE model; new dict placed in error_constants.py alongside the existing maps.

findings.summary: GUARDRAIL_ERROR_TYPE_TO_ERROR_CODE key matching is case-sensitive with no normalization
findings.detail: The dict key is the literal string 'LANGUAGE_VALIDATION'. GuardrailErrorModel.error_type is a plain str with no Literal validator or .upper() normalization before the .get() call at errors.py:451. If the upstream gateway ever delivers 'language_validation' (lowercase) or any other casing variant, the lookup silently returns the CONTENT_POLICY_VIOLATION fallback instead of LANGUAGE_VALIDATION_ERROR. Current provider examples consistently use SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE, so the observed risk is low, but the contract is implicit.

findings.summary: Commit message missing required EPMCDME-14407: ticket prefix
findings.detail: git-workflow.md rule: 'Use EPMCDME-####: Description for repository commits.' The commit message 'Add error message for LANGUAGE_VALIDATION' has no Jira ticket prefix. Correct form: 'EPMCDME-14407: Add dedicated error code for LANGUAGE_VALIDATION guardrail errors'.

finding_status.evidence: No normalization of error_type before dict lookup confirmed by reading errors.py:451 and GuardrailErrorModel definition. Accepted as low risk given provider schema convention; recommended fix: add .upper() before .get() or use a Literal type for GuardrailErrorModel.error_type.

git log --oneline shows commit 8b522b0af 'Add error message for LANGUAGE_VALIDATION' with no EPMCDME-14407: prefix. Non-blocking for merge; should be addressed in a follow-up amend or noted in MR description.
